Morgan P (People Ops): Congrats, @Devon! Quick question about timing — do you want your parental/FMLA leave to start on the baby's birth date or delay a week for recovery?
Raj S (Eng Manager): either works for the team, just need coverage for on-call the week after birth. who can pick that up?
Devon L (IC): I was planning to start leave on birth date but might prefer to delay 5 days if recovery is rough (c-section potential). How does that affect STD/FMLA paperwork?
Samantha (People Ops): You can elect a deferred FMLA start up to X days in some cases, but STD (short-term disability) usually uses the medical leave start date. We need the physician/hospital note to set STD start.
Morgan P (People Ops): Practical steps: 1) fill out the Parental Leave form in the HR portal (link: https://hr.redwood.example/leave) 2) upload hospital note or birth certificate copy (if available) 3) STD claim if applicable (we can help).
Devon L (IC): ok — is a hospital discharge summary ok if certificate isn't issued yet?
Samantha (People Ops): Yes — hospital discharge or infant birth letter works as interim proof. We need official birth certificate within 90 days for benefits reconciliation.
Raj S (Eng Manager): For coverage: I can move my schedule to pick up on-call for the first 3 days, but we need someone for the follow-up rotations. @Morgan can you ping people eng for voluntary swaps?
Morgan P (People Ops): Will post a rotation swap message in #eng-oncall now. Also we can set up temporary contractor coverage if needed — ask your manager to include budget note.
Devon L (IC): payroll/pay codes — how will pay look if I delay FMLA start 5 days but use PTO for those days?
Samantha (People Ops): If you use PTO for the deferred days, mark those as PTO in the portal. FMLA protection can be designated to start later; STD typically starts on the medical leave start date and will coordinate with payroll to offset PTO.
Morgan P (People Ops): Quick checklist I'm sending: 1) Submit leave request in portal 2) Upload hospital note / discharge letter 3) File STD claim (if medical leave) 4) Confirm PTO top-up with manager if delaying FMLA 5) Sign parental leave acknowledgement form. I can DM the doc templates.
HR-Bot: Ticket #HR-4821 created for Devon L. Assigned to Samantha (People Ops). Due: 7 days.
Devon L (IC): thanks — can you share a short handover template? don't want to write a novel.
Raj S (Eng Manager): here's a tiny template I use: ```- status: current sprint tasks (blocked/next) - oncall notes: runbook links & escalation - PRs: links and owners - recurring meetings to skip - contact: backup for urgent decisions```
Morgan P (People Ops): I'll attach a sample handover in the ticket and DM you the forms. We can also do a 15-min sync with you + manager + people ops before leave starts.
Samantha (People Ops): One more policy note: if you eventually request intermittent leave within 12 months, let us know — that requires updated medical documentation.
Devon L (IC): super helpful, thank you. I'll submit portal form tonight and upload the hospital note after birth. Appreciate the coverage help! :heart:
Raj S (Eng Manager): big congrats again, Devon. we'll sort the rota. :raised_hands:
Morgan P (People Ops): Marking action items in ticket and will follow up once forms are in. Reach out anytime.
